### Key Tornado Facts for Illinois

Top insights and patterns from the historical tornado data, revealing the most important statistics about tornado activity in this region.

Average **18.0** tornadoes per year (**82.6/yr** in last decade)

**May** is the peak tornado month with **812** recorded events (**21.3%**)

Most tornadoes occur around **5 PM** (**14.3%** of events)

Deadliest tornado: **F4** in **MOULTRIE, ILLINOIS, 1917** • **101** deaths, **638** injuries

**2024** was the most active year with **175** tornadoes

**MCLEAN** County has the most tornadoes (**129** events, **3.4%**)

Longest tornado: **112.9 miles** in **ADAMS, ILLINOIS, 1938**

Widest tornado: **2,630 yards** (**1.49 miles**) in **FULTON, ILLINOIS, 1975**

Most tornadoes in one day: **61** on **Jul 15, 2024**

### Tornado Analysis and Trends

Detailed charts and visualizations revealing tornado patterns by intensity, seasonality, and impact. These analytics show historical trends and unique characteristics of tornado activity in this region.

#### Monthly Distribution

Shows tornado frequency across different months of the year, highlighting seasonal patterns. This information helps identify peak tornado seasons and periods of heightened risk.

*   Tornados

**Summary:** In Illinois, May is the most active month with 812 tornadoes (21% of all recorded events). The primary tornado season occurs during May, April, June, accounting for 59% of all tornadoes in this region.

#### Time of Day Analysis

Reveals the hourly pattern of tornado occurrence, showing when tornadoes are most likely to strike. Late afternoon and early evening (3-7 PM) are peak tornado hours, while nighttime tornadoes are rare but especially dangerous.⏰ All times shown in local time for Illinois.

*   Tornadoes

**Summary:** In Illinois, tornado activity peaks at **5:00 PM** with 544 tornadoes (14.3% of all events). The afternoon hours (2-7 PM) account for **60%** of all tornadoes, making this the most dangerous time of day. Only **15%** of tornadoes occur at night (10 PM - 6 AM), but nighttime tornadoes are particularly dangerous because people are less likely to receive warnings while sleeping.

#### Tornado Count by County

Identifies the counties most frequently affected by tornadoes in Illinois. This geographical breakdown helps pinpoint tornado hotspots and vulnerable areas.

*   Tornado Count

**Summary:**MCLEAN has experienced the highest number of tornadoes (129) in Illinois, accounting for 3.4% of all tornado events in this state. The top three most tornado-prone counties (MCLEAN, WILL, and SANGAMON) account for 9% of all tornado activity.

#### Annual Tornado Trends

Shows tornado frequency by year with both actual annual counts (bars) and a 5-year moving average (line) to reveal long-term trends. The moving average helps smooth out year-to-year variations, making it easier to identify patterns and changes over time.

#### Tornado Intensity Distribution

Shows the breakdown of tornadoes by intensity rating (EF/F scale). Vertical bars make it easy to compare the prevalence of different tornado strengths, with counts and percentages displayed above each bar.

**Summary:** In Illinois, EF0 tornadoes are the most common, comprising 37.4% of all recorded events. Weak tornadoes (EF0-EF1) account for 67.6% of all events, while strong tornadoes (EF2-EF3) make up 24.5%. Violent tornadoes (EF4-EF5) are relatively rare at only 2.6% of all events, but cause disproportionate damage and casualties.

Note: 5.2% of tornadoes have unknown intensity (FU), typically from historical records where damage assessments were not available.

## Tornado Archive: Historical Tornado Statistics & Facts

Comprehensive database of tornado events in United States recorded since 1680 through the end of 2025(87,477 total records)

### Data Sources

1680-1949: Thomas P. Grazulis Collection

_Significant Tornadoes 1680-1991_, digitized by [TornadoArchive](https://tornadoarchive.com/). Covers F2+ tornadoes and deadly F1s. Historical tracks are approximate based on start/end coordinates.

1950-Present: NOAA Storm Events Database

Official records from [NOAA's National Centers for Environmental Information](https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/stormevents/). All confirmed tornadoes (EF0-EF5) with comprehensive damage and casualty data.

### Key Tornado Facts for Illinois

Top insights and patterns from the historical tornado data, revealing the most important statistics about tornado activity in this region.

Average **18.0** tornadoes per year (**82.6/yr** in last decade)

**May** is the peak tornado month with **812** recorded events (**21.3%**)

Most tornadoes occur around **5 PM** (**14.3%** of events)

Deadliest tornado: **F4** in **MOULTRIE, ILLINOIS, 1917** • **101** deaths, **638** injuries

**2024** was the most active year with **175** tornadoes

**MCLEAN** County has the most tornadoes (**129** events, **3.4%**)

Longest tornado: **112.9 miles** in **ADAMS, ILLINOIS, 1938**

Widest tornado: **2,630 yards** (**1.49 miles**) in **FULTON, ILLINOIS, 1975**

Most tornadoes in one day: **61** on **Jul 15, 2024**

### Key Tornado Facts for Illinois

Top insights and patterns from the historical tornado data, revealing the most important statistics about tornado activity in this region.

Average **18.0** tornadoes per year (**82.6/yr** in last decade)

**May** is the peak tornado month with **812** recorded events (**21.3%**)

Most tornadoes occur around **5 PM** (**14.3%** of events)

Deadliest tornado: **F4** in **MOULTRIE, ILLINOIS, 1917** • **101** deaths, **638** injuries

**2024** was the most active year with **175** tornadoes

**MCLEAN** County has the most tornadoes (**129** events, **3.4%**)

Longest tornado: **112.9 miles** in **ADAMS, ILLINOIS, 1938**

Widest tornado: **2,630 yards** (**1.49 miles**) in **FULTON, ILLINOIS, 1975**

Most tornadoes in one day: **61** on **Jul 15, 2024**
